guardian.description:
Move comes in response to Rome imposing similar measures after mass migration rush to Ceuta

Spain has announced it will introduce temporary border checks on visitors from Italy in response to Rome imposing similar measures after a mass rush of people from Morocco into Ceuta.

The checks, which come “amid the persistent irregular migration pressure” facing Italy, will start at midnight on Saturday and last until 7 September, Spain’s interior ministry said in a statement.

Africa’s public health watchdog said the time for incremental action was over as they announced plans to scale up every aspect of the response and go “door to door” looking for patients.

guardian.description:
Observatory says 36.9C posted on Sunday is city’s highest official temperature since its records began 142 years ago, with storm driving intense heat in region

Hong Kong has officially recorded its highest ever temperature as Typhoon Dolphin swept warm air over the city, the meteorological service said.

The city’s weather observatory posted a temperature of 36.9C on Sunday, the highest recorded since records began in 1884, the Hong Kong Observatory said in the afternoon.

rfi.title: Former Syrian leader Assad sentenced to death in absentia over war crimes

rfi.title: France and EU join international aid effort after Colombia earthquake
rfi.description: France has joined the European Union and a host of countries in offering assistance to Colombia, where volunteers and rescuers are searching for survivors following Monday's deadly earthquake.

rfi.description: Rebel authorities on Tuesday accused the Ethiopian government of carrying out deadly drone strikes in southern Tigray state and condemned the move as "a serious escalation", amid fears of a new war.

rfi.title: Ghana backs Jamaica's petition to push UK for slavery reparations
rfi.description: Jamaica and Ghana, both former British colonies subjected to the transatlantic slave trade, are presenting a united front in the drive for reparatory justice. As Kingston prepares to lodge a formal petition with King Charles III seeking to advance its claim for reparations from the United Kingdom, Ghana's president says the global movement to address the legacy of slavery has reached a "defining moment".

rfi.title: Outsiders Malawi beat Ghana to reach WAFCON semi-finals and World Cup

rfi.title: As the planet heats up, butterflies are seeking out cooler climes
rfi.description: Climate change is driving shifts in where butterflies are found globally, according to a major new study, with some species moving northwards or seeking out higher elevations in search of cooler conditions.

rfi.title: Demi Vollering wins Women's Tour de France for the second time
rfi.description: Dutch cyclist Demi Vollering on Sunday won her second Women’s Tour de France title, dethroning defending champion Pauline Ferrand-Prévot from France, who dropped out of the race on Saturday. Vollering excelled during the hilly final stage to extend her lead on nearest rival Katarzyna Niewiadoma-Phinney, who finished second overall.

Chinese mining group CMOC, which owns the main site examined in Katanga, disputes the findings.

rfi.description: Electric scooter riders in Paris must now wear helmets and reflective gear under new rules introduced after a significant rise in injuries involving the two-wheelers, police said at the weekend.

rfi.title: Sall's chances at UN secretary-general role weakened after first vote
rfi.description: Antonio Guterres’s successor as United Nations secretary-general will be named in October. So far, two candidates from the African continent – Senegal’s Macky Sall and Uganda’s Olara Otunnu – have failed to win sufficient support.

rfi.title: Morocco, Algeria reach WAFCON semi-finals and World Cup

Gewalt in der S-Bahn: Blut auf der Heimfahrt
zeit.description: Ein Familienausflug ins Stadion endet in einer Prügelei in der S-Bahn. ZEIT-Chefreporter Stefan Willeke fragt: Warum eskaliert Gewalt – und warum immer wieder im Fußball?

zeit.title: Schwangerschaftsabbrüche in den USA: Massachusetts legalisiert Schwangerschaftsabbrüche nach der 24. Woche
zeit.description: Als zehnter Bundesstaat lockert Massachusetts die Regelungen zu Schwangerschaftsabbrüchen. Der von den Demokraten regierte Staat stellt sich damit gegen die US-Regierung.

zeit.title: Vulkanausbruch auf Sizilien: Ätna stößt große Mengen Asche und Gesteinsbrocken aus
zeit.description: Mitten in der Hauptreisezeit sorgt Europas aktivster Vulkan auf Sizilien für große Probleme. In Catania konnte am Morgen nur eine einzige Maschine starten.

zeit.title: Mekka-Verteidigungspakt: Ein Militärbündnis nach Mekka zu benennen? Ein dreistes Symbol
zeit.description: Mekka steht für die Einheit aller Muslime. Saudi-Arabien, die Türkei und Pakistan nutzen die Autorität des Ortes nun für ein Bündnis – eine folgenreiche Entscheidung.

zeit.title: Social-Media-Verbot: Sollte der Staat Social Media für unter 16-Jährige verbieten?
zeit.description: Soziale Medien können ein schrecklicher Ort sein, vor allem für Jugendliche. Aber ein Verbot löst das Problem nicht. Und es übersieht, wofür TikTok und Co. wichtig sind.

zeit.title: »The Shards«: Wie man Bret Easton Ellis nicht verfilmt
zeit.description: Schon mal ein Beutelchen Koks gekauft, das sich als Milchpulver herausgestellt hat? Mit »The Shards« hat Disney+ das Gefühl dieser Enttäuschung zu einer Serie gemacht.

zeit.title: Niedrigwasser: Auch Hamburg und Schleswig-Holstein heben Lkw-Fahrverbot auf
zeit.description: Angesichts des Niedrigwassers in vielen Flüssen setzen immer mehr Bundesländer das Sonntagsfahrverbot aus. Nun ziehen auch Schleswig-Holstein und Hamburg mit.

observador.title: Inglaterra poderá erradicar hepatite C antes de 2030
observador.description: País está próximo de cumprir meta da OMS de tratar 80% dos casos diagnosticados até final da década.. Mais de 100 mil pessoas foram diagnosticadas e tratadas para a doença desde 2015.

observador.title: Os 10 terramotos mais mortíferos na América Latina
observador.description: A América Latina enfrentou alguns dos sismos mais fortes de que há registo. Entre eles estão o terramoto de 2010 no Haiti e de 1868 no Equador e na Colômbia.

observador.title: Seguro considera que "interior não é um fardo"
observador.description: Nesta visita à Beira Baixa, o Presidente da República defendeu a necessidade de "uma visão estratégica" e de "investimento público que potencie o investimento privado"

observador.title: 14h. Saída de professores para reforma preocupa FENPROF
observador.description: Este ano reformaram-se quase 3.300 docentes, ainda assim foram menos do que no ano passado. Ainda neste jornal, sobe para 224 número de mortos na colômbia na sequência do grande sismo de ontem.

observador.title: 13h. Colômbia. Número de vítimas mortais sobe para 169
observador.description: Há registo de cerca de 1.250 feridos e de mais de 2.700 pessoas dadas como desaparecidas. Ainda nesta edição, António José Seguro defende que o interior não é um fardo, mas precisa de oportunidades.

observador.title: Levantada interdição a banhos na Praia do Areínho em Ovar
observador.description: A Câmara de Ovar, no distrito de Aveiro, garante agora que estão "novamente reunidas condições de qualidade e segurança" para os utilizadores da praia irem a banhos.

observador.title: Câmara das Caldas da Rainha vai apoiar família de bebé
observador.description: O bebé, que caiu de um quarto andar, no Avenal, nas Caldas da Rainha, no distrito de Leiria, morreu no Hospital de Santa Maria, em Lisboa.

observador.title: Setúbal vai compensar quem disponibilizou água a bombeiros
observador.description: Os potenciais beneficiários devem fazer o pedido de compensação através do endereço de correio eletrónico apoiocliente@sms-setubal.pt.

observador.title: João Soares, Portas e Mesquita Nunes na Universidade do PSD
observador.description: Antigo presidente da Câmara de Lisboa, histórico líder do CDS e ex-secretário de Estado juntam-se à iniciativa do PSD em Castelo de Vide, que contará ainda com pesos pesados do partido e do Governo.

observador.title: Bashar al-Assad condenado à pena de morte
observador.description: Antigo Presidente da Síria foi condenado a pena de morte pelo tribunal penal de Damasco, à revelia. Também o irmão e o primo materno foram condenados à mesma pena.

observador.title: Rod Stewart cancela dois concertos por razões médicas
observador.description: Recomendado a manter-se em repouso durante 48 horas, o cantor britânico de 81 anos teve de cancelar atuações marcadas para domingo e esta terça-feira. Rod Stewart atuou em Portugal em junho.

observador.title: Imigração, asilo, retorno e menores: crise à vista? — Debate
observador.description: A Lei do Retorno chega ao Tribunal Constitucional enquanto Governo diz seguir novas regras migratórias e Europa enfrenta fronteiras vulneráveis. E o que está acontecer na imigração com as crianças?

observador.title: Nottingham oficializa acordo com o Sporting por Diomande
observador.description: O defesa central costa-marfinense realizou 132 jogos pelos leões e apontou sete golos — o primeiro num dérbi, diante do Benfica; o último contra o Ath. Bilbao, a contar para a Liga dos Campeões.

observador.title: Incêndios na Indonésia mobilizam mais de 48.000 bombeiros
observador.description: O país do Sudeste Asiático está a viver o início de uma época seca longa e intensa agravada pelo fenómeno climático El Niño.

observador.title: 12h. Colômbia. MNE dá conta de danos em casas de portugueses
observador.description: Até ao momento, não há registo de vítimas mortais ou feridos entre a comunidade portuguesa no país, apenas de danos materiais. Ainda, antigo presidente sírio Bashar al-Assad condenado à pena de morte.

observador.title: Algarve sem "avalanche" e à espera da "última hora"
observador.description: "Não há drama" no turismo algarvio, garantem associações. Hotelaria regista quebra ligeira e menos portugueses, mas não quer concorrer com o "tudo incluído" de Espanha. AL nota descida dos preços.

observador.title: Região de Coimbra estabelece acordo com agência ucraniana
observador.description: As áreas de cooperação são a partilha de conhecimento, de boas práticas e experiências em matérias de desenvolvimento regional, inovação, sustentabilidade, resiliência económica.

observador.title: Obama lança podcast sobre os livros que marcaram a sua vida
observador.description: O antigo presidente dos EUA vai lançar um podcast com seis episódios, disponível na Audible a 24 de setembro. Em cada episódio, Obama recebe um convidado e juntos falam sobre um dos livros escolhidos.

nzz.title: Boxpromoter und mutmasslicher Chef eines Drogenimperiums: Wer ist Daniel Kinahan, Irlands wohl gefährlichster Gangsterboss?
nzz.description: Kinahan soll mit seiner Organisation jahrelang den Drogen- und Waffenschmuggel in Irland und darüber hinaus kontrolliert haben. Nun haben ihn die Vereinigten Arabischen Emirate nach Irland ausgeliefert. Dort droht ihm lebenslange Haft.

nzz.title: ERKLÄRT - Kolumbiens Präsident ruft nach Erdbeben der Stärke 7,4 den Notstand aus: Zahl der Toten steigt auf mehr als 220
nzz.description: Ein starkes Erdbeben hat am Montag Kolumbien erschüttert. Zahlreiche Gebäude stürzten ein und die Zahl der Verletzten könnte sich auf mehrere Hunderte belaufen. Die wichtigsten Antworten.

nzz.title: Libanons Parlament schafft die Todesstrafe ab
nzz.description: Mit der Abschaffung ist der Libanon das erste arabische Land, das die Todesstrafe formell aus seinem Strafrecht streicht. Der Hizbullah stimmte dagegen.

nzz.title: KURZMELDUNGEN - News aus Zürich: Nach Jahren mit roten Zahlen schreibt das Unispital wieder Gewinne
nzz.description: Die neuesten Meldungen aus dem Kanton.

nzz.description: Russland war jahrelang der wichtigste Verbündete des gestürzten Diktators Bashar al-Asad. Trotzdem hat Syriens neue Regierung jetzt ein militärisches Kooperationsabkommen mit Moskau geschlossen. Sie hat dafür gute Gründe.

nzz.description: Das schwere Erdbeben in Kolumbien fordert mindestens 224 Tote und ist eine erste Prüfung für die neue Rechtsregierung. Diese kann indes auf ihre Verbündeten in der Region und in Washington zählen.

nzz.description: Wo ist es zurzeit besonders heiss? Und was sind die Auswirkungen auf die Menschen und die Umwelt? Die neuesten Meldungen über Hitzerekorde, Dürren und Brände in Europa.

nzz.title: Ätna hochaktiv – Tausende Touristen gestrandet
nzz.description: Mitten in der Hauptreisezeit sorgt Europas grösster Vulkan mit seinen Ausbrüchen für grosse Probleme. In Catania kann am Dienstagmorgen nur eine einzige Maschine starten. Touristen sind verzweifelt.

nzz.title: Limmatboot-Rundfahrt wird wegen tiefen Wasserstands per sofort eingestellt
nzz.description: Auch auf dem Zürichsee kommt es zu weiteren Einschränkungen.

nzz.title: «Er ist phantastisch»: Donald Trump springt Gianni Infantino zur Seite
nzz.description: Der amerikanische Präsident lobt den bedrängten Fifa-Präsidenten auf seiner Plattform Truth Social. Es ist eine weitere Episode im offenen Kampf um die Macht im Weltfussball.

nzz.description: Die neuesten Polizeimeldungen aus der Region.

nzz.description: Seit dem Sturz des langjährigen Machthabers Bashar al-Asad Ende 2024 erlebt Syrien ungewisse Zeiten. So zeigt sich zurzeit die Lage.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Der Fall des ehemaligen Raiffeisen-Chefs Pierin Vincenz: «Die Bank führt einen Kampf gegen mich»
nzz.description: Im Zentrum des Berufungsprozesses steht die Frage, ob die gegen Pierin Vincenz verhängte langjährige Freiheitsstrafe gerechtfertigt ist. Alle Entwicklungen im Prozess.

nzz.title: Elf Monate kein Rennen und trotzdem schneller als alle: Jakob Ingebrigtsen gelingt in Birmingham ein Sensations-Comeback, Lobalu geht leer aus
nzz.description: Der 25-jährige Norweger Ingebrigtsen hat in den vergangenen anderthalb Jahren kaum Wettkämpfe bestritten, sich an der Achillessehne operieren lassen und musste vor Gericht eine Niederlage gegen seinen Vater verdauen. An den EM über 5000 Meter spielt das alles keine Rolle mehr.

spiegel.title: Ungarn: Orbán-Kritiker András Baka ist neues Staatsoberhaupt Ungarns
spiegel.description: Ungarn hat einen neuen Präsidenten: Das Parlament in Budapest hat den 73-jährigen András Baka für das Amt des Staatsoberhaupts gewählt. Der Jurist wurde einst von Viktor Orbán aus einem wichtigen Amt abberufen.

spiegel.title: Claude: Chatbot von Anthropic markiert KI-Texte künftiger Modelle mit Wasserzeichen
spiegel.description: Wurde eine E-Mail oder ein Artikel vom KI-Chatbot Claude generiert? In Zukunft könnte sich das leichter herausfinden lassen, dank eines neuen Kennzeichnungssystems, das Anthropic einführt.

spiegel.title: Drohnen-Attacke auf dem Flughafen in Leipzig: So könnte Friedrich Merz Russland abstrafen
spiegel.description: Die Spuren der vereitelten Drohnenattacke auf dem Leipziger Flughafen weisen nach Moskau. Was tut der Kanzler, wenn sich der Verdacht erhärtet? Aus diesen vier Optionen könnte er wählen.

spiegel.title: Libanon schafft die Todesstrafe ab
spiegel.description: Seit 2004 wurde im Libanon niemand mehr hingerichtet, verhängt wurde die Todesstrafe dennoch weiter. Nun ist wegen einer Gesetzesänderung Schluss damit. Unverändert prekär: die Lage in Gefängnissen.

spiegel.title: Julia Klöckner: Kritik an KI-Bild zum Schulstart in Rheinland-Pfalz
spiegel.description: Die Bundestagspräsidentin erntet Kritik, weil sie zum Schuljahresbeginn in Rheinland-Pfalz ein KI-generiertes Bild mit vier Kindern postete. Was daran noch verwundert: die fehlende Vielfalt.

spiegel.title: Leichtathletik-EM: Smilla Kolbe mit schnellster deutscher Zeit über 800 Meter seit der Wiedervereinigung
spiegel.description: Smilla Kolbe hat das bisherige Highlight des zweiten Wettkampftages der Leichtathletik-EM geboten. In ihrem Vorlauf blieb sie als erste deutsche Läuferin seit 1990 unter 1:58 Minuten.

spiegel.title: Auch Hamburg, Hessen und Bayern erlauben Lkw-Verkehr am Wochenende

spiegel.title: Quiz des Tages beim SPIEGEL: 7 Fragen zum Allgemeinwissen pro Tag

spiegel.description: Ein 56-Jähriger erlitt in Bremen tödliche Kopfverletzungen. Zuvor soll er von einem Autofahrer geschlagen worden sein. Bei der Fahndung nach dem Tatverdächtigen haben die Ermittler nun ein Hinweisportal eingerichtet.

spiegel.title: Hannover sperrte Flughafen wegen Drohnensichtung
spiegel.description: Zwei Stunden lang ist die Polizei in der vergangenen Nacht einer Drohne hinterhergejagt. Weil sie sich mit der Ortungstechnik der Bundespolizei nicht entdecken ließ, schließen die Ermittler eine neue »hybride Aktivität« nicht aus.

spiegel.title: Fitness: Viel Protein ist gut, mehr Protein ist besser? Falsch
spiegel.description: Eiweiß in Shakes, in Riegeln, in Fleisch: Neben Kraftsportlern sollen Läufer oder Radfahrer ebenfalls davon profitieren. Wann Proteine auch im Ausdauersport helfen und was der schnelle Shake nach dem Training bringt.

spiegel.title: Dressurreiten: Isabell Werth kritisiert Debattenkultur im Netz scharf
spiegel.description: Kurz vor der Reit-WM in Deutschland prangert Rekordsiegerin Isabell Werth die Diskussionsweise der Pferdesportgegner in sozialen Medien an. Dabei ist essenziell, dass Sportler und Tierschützer weiter miteinander reden.

spiegel.title: Verehrung von Josef Stalin im heutigen Russland unter Wladimir Putin: Wie der Kreml-Chef den Massenmörder Stalin rehabiliert
spiegel.description: Für Machthaber Wladimir Putin verkörpert Josef Stalin die imperiale Größe, die er selbst anstrebt. Wer heute in Russland an die Verbrechen des Sowjetdiktators erinnert, wird zum Staatsfeind erklärt.

spiegel.title: Magersucht und Bulimie: Zahl der betroffenen Mädchen in 20 Jahren verdoppelt
spiegel.description: Von Essstörungen wie Bulimie und Magersucht sind vorwiegend Mädchen und junge Frauen betroffen – Tendenz steigend. 2024 mussten fast 6000 von ihnen in einer Klinik behandelt werden.

spiegel.title: Thüringen: Mario Voigt scheitert mit Einspruch gegen Entzug seines Doktortitels
spiegel.description: Seit Jahren gibt es Plagiatsvorwürfe gegen Mario Voigt. Die TU Chemnitz ist dem nachgegangen und bleibt nach Prüfung dabei, Thüringens Regierungschef den Doktorgrad zu entziehen. Er will nun rechtliche Schritte einleiten.

spiegel.title: Perseiden: Sommer-Sternschnuppen erreichen in der Nacht ihren Höhepunkt
spiegel.description: Der 12. August bietet nicht nur eine Sonnenfinsternis: In der mondlosen Nacht zu Donnerstag zünden die Perseiden ein Sternschnuppenfeuerwerk am Himmel.

spiegel.title: Iran: Mohsen Rezaee ist der neue Chef des Nationalen Sicherheitsrats
spiegel.description: Er hat die Revolutionswächter befehligt, ist Hardliner, und die argentinische Justiz wirft ihm Terrorismus vor: Mohsen Rezaee übernimmt als oberster Sicherheitsberater in Iran. Nachgiebigkeit dürfen die USA von ihm nicht erwarten.

spiegel.description: Unter der Intendantin Shermin Langhoff lieferte das Berliner Maxim Gorki Theater enorme Impulse für den Umbau der deutschsprachigen Theaterwelt. Ihre Nachfolgerin Çağla Ilk verkündet nun eine knallharte Disruption.

undark.title: Book Review: How Wildlife Is Returning to the East
undark.description: In “The Beasts of the East,” journalist Andrew Moore charts the natural history of the East and the people who have dedicated their careers to restoring several long lost species to what remains of their original habitats.

undark.title: Book Review: The Case for the AI-Powered Global Brain
undark.description: In “The God Test,” Robert Wright considers a future in which human consciousness becomes infused with AI. “We have to think seriously about a future in which there is something that increasingly resembles a global brain, and its neurons increasingly consist not just of human brains but of AIs,” he writes.

undark.title: Interview: How Tragedy Changed the FDA
undark.description: As an FDA advisory committee prepares to weigh whether specialized pharmacies should be allowed to dispense seven unapproved peptides, Mikkael A. Sekeres, a scientist and former adviser, discusses the history and nuances of FDA oversight, including its process for screening advisory committee members for conflicts of interest.

undark.title: Will AI Fix Prior Authorization — or Make It Worse?
undark.description: The Trump administration is currently piloting a program in six states that expands Medicare prior authorizations using AI tools in an effort to reduce unnecessary medical spending. But it remains to be seen whether this new approach, which the administration has called “broken” in the private sector, will be effective without causing dangerous delays for Medicare recipients.

undark.title: Biologists Should Articulate Their Position on AI
undark.description: Last month, mathematics researchers released the Leiden Declaration, a treatise on how to handle the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to their field. C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that biologists should learn from the mathematics community and work on their own version.

undark.title: Review: What Animals Can Teach Humans About Caregiving
undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

undark.title: The MAHA Movement’s Worrisome Embrace of Ibogaine
undark.description: The MAHA movement has been promoting the plant-based substance ibogaine as a remedy for opioid addiction, despite the lack of clinical trials on its safety and efficacy. One physician who practices addiction medicine discusses the risks of ibogaine and argues for the need to support proven treatments.

undark.title: Advocacy Groups Express Mixed Views on Embryo Editing
undark.description: At least two new start-up companies, Preventive and Origin Genomics, say they are developing strategies that combine gene editing with in vitro fertilization to correct disease-causing mutations. Advocacy groups for people living with these genetic disorders have been quiet on the developments.

undark.title: Interview: California Lawmaker Calls for a Peptide Working Group
undark.description: Amid a national push to ease restrictions on certain peptides, California legislator Joe Patterson has introduced a state-level bill that would to establish a working group tasked with making recommendations to allow physicians and hospitals, among others, to prescribe and study promising peptides.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

phys-org.title: Opposition to local data centers rises sharply, survey finds
phys-org.description: As protesters rally against data center construction in dozens of states and New York and Texas pause the issuance of permits for large data centers, a new nationally representative survey finds that Americans' opposition to data centers in their communities has risen sharply since last spring.

phys-org.title: Researchers develop new framework for understanding how emotions shape behavior online
phys-org.description: Every day, billions of people scroll through social media posts, online reviews and news feeds filled with emotional content—from glowing five-star reviews to rage-inducing social media rants. Those emotions can quietly shape what people buy, what they believe and how they act.

phys-org.title: Decoding smell: Study reveals how wind transforms odor signals
phys-org.description: Humans trust dogs to help find missing people, and bees to pollinate their crops. But scientists still don't fully understand how these animals use their extraordinary sense of smell to locate the source of an odor.

phys-org.title: A smarter way to track satellites beyond Earth's orbit
phys-org.description: Most current space activities operate close to Earth in what is called near–Earth orbit. However, as more satellites and other infrastructure begin to extend beyond that region, maintaining situational awareness of those objects will be crucial.

phys-org.title: Color-sensing yeast could make biofactories more programmable and precise
phys-org.description: Baker's yeast is one of biotechnology's most important microorganisms. It has long been used to leaven bread and ferment beer. More recently, advances in synthetic biology have enabled engineered yeast to convert sugar into a wide range of products, including medicines, fuels and industrial chemicals. Yet even well-engineered yeast cells can be difficult to control in a precise and timely way.

phys-org.title: Want a happier marriage? Study suggests one simple habit
phys-org.description: Research has long shown that exercise benefits both physical and mental health. Now, a new study from researchers at BYU suggests that it may also strengthen marriages, especially when couples exercise together.

phys-org.title: Australia's plastic exports may deepen health risks in Indonesian communities
phys-org.description: A new commentary in BMJ Global Health, co-authored by the George Institute, reveals that Australia exported 22,333 metric tons of plastic waste to Indonesia in 2023–24 alone, part of a wider crisis that has seen the country take in more than 200,000 metric tons of imported waste it cannot safely process. Up to 80% of it ends up burned or dumped.

phys-org.title: How barramundi research gives breeders more control
phys-org.description: Barramundi farmers will soon be able to improve stock genetics by placing more emphasis on the sex of their breeding fish. University of Queensland Ph.D. candidate Jessica Hintzsche has produced the most detailed genetic map ever created for barramundi, showing how traits can be passed between generations.

phys-org.title: Historical DNA reveals largetooth sawfish have lost much of their genetic diversity
phys-org.description: The genetic diversity of the largetooth sawfish (Pristis pristis), a critically endangered ray, has plummeted over the past century and a half, according to a study published in the Proceedings of the Royal Society B: Biological Sciences. The species once lived in tropical waters worldwide but has disappeared from much of its former range.

phys-org.title: Large-scale study finds no link between crime and unauthorized immigration
phys-org.description: For more than two decades, Charis E. Kubrin has followed the data wherever it leads. As UC Irvine Chancellor's Professor of Criminology, Law and Society, she has built a career studying one of America's most politically charged questions: Does immigration drive crime?

phys-org.title: In Oregon, voters' passage of gun control measure led to more firearms in the state
phys-org.description: Oregon voters' narrow 2022 approval of a referendum designed to limit gun purchases has instead resulted in thousands more firearms in the state than there otherwise would have been, a new analysis suggests.

phys-org.title: First evidence of Neanderthal bone tool use in Romania discovered
phys-org.description: Deep in the Vârghiș Gorges, tucked away in the dark recesses of a cave, researchers have found the first evidence that Neanderthals used bone tools in Romania.

phys-org.title: Fighting pathogens by watching how they read their own DNA: Q&A with structural biologist
phys-org.description: Every living cell, from the simplest bacterium to a human neuron, relies on the same basic machinery to read, interpret, and use its DNA. This molecular machinery is so fundamental that life as we know it cannot exist without it. And because it is so essential, it has long been a target for drugs; it shuts down a bacterium's ability to access its own genes and it quickly dies.

phys-org.title: Who are the secret gardeners of a parasitic plant?
phys-org.description: In the coastal forests of a tropical Japanese island near Okinawa grows an inconspicuous plant that is easy to mistake for a mushroom. It is a non-green parasite that feeds on the roots of other plants and produces up to 1 million tiny seeds, each covered in a minuscule, dry fruit. The seeds, in particular, present a mystery to scientists: How do they get dispersed?

phys-org.title: Ancient Colombians built huge water system without centralized rule, archaeologists say
phys-org.description: Communities living in Colombia thousands of years ago achieved an engineering wonder of the world based on cooperation among family groups without top-down government, a new study shows. Archaeologists argue that policymakers in Colombia should now adopt a similar strategy to solve the country's current water management crisis.

phys-org.title: New optical method reveals internal dynamics of elusive Wigner crystals
phys-org.description: Researchers at the University of Basel and the Technical University of Munich have developed a new method to reveal the collective motion of electrons in one of the most elusive states of matter: the Wigner crystal. Using light, the physicists were able to uncover previously inaccessible properties of this fragile quantum state.

phys-org.title: Jackie, the California bald eagle who became an internet sensation, dies after illness
phys-org.description: Jackie, the bald eagle who became an internet sensation and a symbol of the species' recovery in California, died Monday after being treated for an illness at a veterinary facility, her caretakers announced.

phys-org.title: Magnitude 7.4 quake rocks western Colombia, killing at least 111 people
phys-org.description: A powerful 7.4 magnitude earthquake struck western Colombia on Monday, killing at least 111 people, damaging hundreds of buildings and leaving many trapped under debris while their loved ones and rescue workers searched through rubble.

proj-syn.title: Dude, Where’s My Recession?
proj-syn.description: Despite a series of major negative shocks, some of them unprecedented, the US economy continues to grow in line with its estimated long-run potential. Yet given obvious and mounting risks, from debt-financed speculation to geopolitical tensions, the appearance of resilience should not be confused with the real thing.

proj-syn.title: The Token Economy Requires Collective Data Governance
proj-syn.description: Millions of people continuously generate the raw material on which AI is trained, yet almost none shares in the wealth it creates. This underscores the need for data cooperatives representing internet users, creators, and other rights holders to negotiate access to the content being fed to large language models.

proj-syn.title: Excess Savings Are Driving the New China Shock
proj-syn.description: The current China shock combines continued supply upgrading with an absorption problem: the decline in property and related investment has reduced domestic demand, but national saving remains very high. The result is a larger savings-investment surplus that spills into net exports.

proj-syn.title: The World Economy Is Swerving, and the Destination Is Unknown
proj-syn.description: The days of unfettered globalization, multilateral rule of law, commonly accepted limits on economic statecraft, and widely shared macroeconomic objectives are now long gone. A perpetual, directionless transition is our new reality, and corporate executives, investors, and policymakers must adapt accordingly.

proj-syn.title: Is China Really a Beggar-thy-Neighbor Power?
proj-syn.description: When major economies are running at near full capacity, it is not clear that trade deficits should be a cause for concern, since they represent a transfer of purchasing power from surplus countries. Under the current circumstances, then, China’s widely criticized surpluses might as well be called enrich-thy-neighbor.

proj-syn.title: No Escape from the Russian Terror Playbook
proj-syn.description: When Vladimir Putin revives Stalin-era repression tactics, he does not do so in service of some lofty ideology or grand project. Rather, he and his security apparatus are seeking to safeguard their own power indefinitely—and, as Russians well know, they will stop at nothing to succeed.

proj-syn.title: The Extractive Trap Has a Green Exit
proj-syn.description: For resource-rich developing countries, decades of resource extraction have produced income concentration, economic dependency, external vulnerabilities, and the weakening of other productive sectors. Achieving broad-based prosperity requires a new approach, one which leverages South-South cooperation to build green industries.

proj-syn.title: The Last Trump Election
proj-syn.description: No matter what US President Donald Trump says or does in response to the results of this November’s midterms, he will have faced his final popular vote. There will be further damage done to public confidence in American democratic institutions, but the institutions themselves will hold.

proj-syn.title: The Ceuta Crisis Is About More Than Migration
proj-syn.description: When tens of thousands of people recently entered the Spanish enclave of Ceuta from neighboring Morocco, European leaders lapsed into recriminations, reigniting the debate on migration. But the bigger challenge is to address a long-simmering territorial dispute between Spain and Morocco.

proj-syn.title: The Rising Price of a Cheap Renminbi
proj-syn.description: Renminbi appreciation would not, on its own, rebalance China’s economy and eliminate its massive surpluses. But by increasing households’ purchasing power over imports and compressing tradable-sector margins, it would raise the cost of avoiding reform.

proj-syn.title: Who Should Build the Low-Carbon Economy?
proj-syn.description: Since the first Industrial Revolution, goods and technologies have reached the farthest corners of the world, but the ability to design, build, market, and extract value from them has remained highly concentrated. Unless humanity can break this pattern, a sufficient response to climate change will remain out of reach.

proj-syn.title: Will Iceland Rejoin the EU Path?
proj-syn.description: US President Donald Trump’s volatile and unpredictable security policies, particularly his desire to control Greenland, have put Iceland in a vulnerable position. This uncomfortable reality will likely be front of mind as voters decide whether to reopen membership negotiations with the European Union.

proj-syn.title: Democracy, Autocracy, or Something Else?
proj-syn.description: Contrary to conventional wisdom, the world is neither converging on liberal democracy nor being swept by an authoritarian tide. The decisive political struggles of the 21st century will be won or lost through the unglamorous work of strengthening democratic accountability and building effective institutions.

proj-syn.title: Colombia’s New Right-Wing Government Faces an Uphill Battle
proj-syn.description: Colombian President-elect Abelardo de la Espriella inherits an economy constrained by weak investment and a severe fiscal crisis. His ability to restore fiscal stability without sacrificing the social gains of recent decades will determine whether the country’s rightward shift proves lasting or short-lived.

proj-syn.title: Can Progressives Deliver Economic Growth?
proj-syn.description: At a time of historic inequality and inadequate public investment, the kind of redistributive policies promoted by politicians on the left are badly needed. But given that no jurisdiction can tax and regulate its way to affordability, a growth-enhancing agenda that generates good jobs and productive capacity is also vital.

proj-syn.title: Fauci’s Modern Pillory
proj-syn.description: MAGA Republicans’ decision to drag Anthony Fauci before a Senate hearing was less about their hatred of science and more about their disdain for the scientists who guide lawmakers in their decision-making. They couldn’t wait to pillory him, and by association any public-facing expert, in front of the cameras.

proj-syn.title: Cheaper Mortgages Won’t Solve the US Housing Crisis
proj-syn.description: For decades, federal housing policy has favored cheaper financing over expanding the housing supply, despite evidence that expanding mortgage credit increases borrowing and house prices. The bipartisan 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act marks an important shift by emphasizing measures that make it easier to build more homes.

proj-syn.title: The Right Way to Regulate AI
proj-syn.description: Governments tend to treat AI as a national-security challenge while devoting far less attention to its effects on education, health, labor markets, and the judiciary. Addressing AI’s societal risks requires institutions designed to recognize and respond to emerging threats before they become systemic failures.

crunchbase.title: AI-Native, Not AI-Sprinkle: Why AI Is A Business Change, Not A Technology Change
crunchbase.description: Companies unlock AI’s biggest productivity gains not by adding AI tools to existing workflows, but by redesigning teams, roles and daily work around AI. The broader lesson, argues Bob Morse, co-founder and managing partner of Strattam Capital, is that achieving transformational gains like 3x productivity requires CEO- and board-backed organizational change — not merely technology adoption.

crunchbase.title: The Biggest Consequence Of An AI IPO Isn’t The IPO Itself. It’s What Happens Afterward.

That capital is likely to flow disproportionately to the largest, established VC firms, writes guest author Andrew Gershfeld of Flint Capital, creating a concentration flywheel that could reshape fundraising, startup financing and power across the venture ecosystem.
